sections.html:
Littleton is a home rule city and the county seat of Arapahoe County, about 9 miles south of downtown Denver. Small parts of the city extend into Jefferson County and Douglas County.

The city covers roughly 13.8 square miles at an elevation of 5,397 feet and had 45,652 residents at the 2020 census, which ranked it 20th among Colorado municipalities. It sits along the South Platte River, with most of the city on the east side of the river. Denver and Englewood border it on the north, Greenwood Village on the northeast, Centennial on the east, Highlands Ranch on the south and Columbine on the west.

Because the city touches three counties, the county that bills your property tax and records your deed depends on which part of Littleton the house sits in.

sections.h2: Is my Littleton address actually inside the city of Littleton?
sections.html:
Not always. The Littleton name is assigned to eleven ZIP codes that cover a far larger area than the city itself, so many houses with a Littleton mailing address are outside the city limits.

Unincorporated areas that use the Littleton name include Columbine, Ken Caryl, Roxborough Park, Heritage Hills and Acres Green, and Highlands Ranch is also allowed in mailing addresses. The city's own page tells owners to use its Address Wizard and city limits map to confirm. This is why Columbine High School, which many people associate with Littleton, is in the Jeffco school district and in an unincorporated area.

  • Inside city limits: Littleton city rules, permits and rental registration apply.
  • Outside city limits: the county or another town applies instead.
  • Not sure: check the city's Address Wizard before you list or request an offer.

When we review a Littleton property, we confirm which jurisdiction it falls under before anything else.

Littleton traces back to the 1859 Pike's Peak gold rush, which drew merchants and farmers along with gold seekers. Richard Sullivan Little, an engineer from New Hampshire who came west to work on irrigation, settled the area and brought his wife Angeline in 1862.

The Littles and their neighbors built the Rough and Ready Flour Mill in 1867, giving the community an economic base. By 1890 the population was 245, and residents voted to incorporate on March 13, 1890. Growth jumped in the 1950s and 1960s, driven by proximity to Denver and the nearby Martin Marietta facilities that produced the Titan rocket.

The population went from 3,378 in 1950 to 13,670 in 1960 and 26,466 in 1970. The city's growth in those decades is the backdrop for much of its older housing.

sections.h2: What do Littleton's census numbers show?
sections.html:
The table below summarizes the 2020 census.

About a third of Littleton households were one-person households, and 12.8 percent were someone age 65 or older living alone. With a median age near 41 and nearly a fifth of residents 65 or older, selling to downsize, relocate or settle an estate is a realistic scenario for many owners.

sections.h2: Do Littleton landlords need to register rental property?
sections.html:
Yes, if you own a multifamily property with three or more units inside the city. Littleton requires a Rental Registration License, adopted under city ordinance 3-19-2 on December 15, 1998.

Property sizeAnnual fee per property
3 to 25 units$75
26 or more units$125

Licenses run one year and renew by April 1, with a separate application and fee for each parcel. Owners must name an agent who lives in the Denver metro area and can authorize emergency repairs and let a city inspector in.

The city's page also covers sales. The seller should notify the city of the pending change of ownership, and the new owner must register within 30 days after the transfer. If you own a small apartment building in Littleton and want to sell, ask your title company to include the city notice in the closing checklist. Details are on the Littleton rental registration page, and the Permit Center can be reached at 303-795-3751.

Most of the Arapahoe County portion of Littleton is in Littleton Public Schools. Heritage High School, Littleton High School and Arapahoe High School are the three high schools inside city limits.

Small portions of the city belong to other districts. The Sheridan School District 2 and Englewood School District 1 cover slivers of the Arapahoe County side, the Jefferson County part falls in Jeffco Public Schools, and the Douglas County part is in Douglas County School District RE-1. If a buyer cares about a specific school, point them to the district's boundary tools rather than a general statement, since the right answer depends on the block.

Arapahoe Community College and Denver Seminary are located in the city, and AdventHealth Littleton is the only hospital.

sections.h2: How do Littleton roads and light rail work?
sections.html:
Four highways run through Littleton, and two RTD light rail stations serve it. The highways are listed below.

  • US 85, South Santa Fe Drive, runs the length of the city from Englewood in the north to Highlands Ranch in the south.
  • State Highway 75, South Platte Canyon Road, begins at West Bowles Avenue and runs south into Columbine Valley.
  • State Highway 88, East Belleview Avenue, runs near the northern edge.
  • State Highway 470 runs along the southern edge.

Light rail began serving Littleton on July 14, 2000. Littleton-Downtown station sits in the historic downtown, and Littleton-Mineral station near the Aspen Grove shopping center is the southern end of the D Line. Littleton also shares Denver's house numbering grid, even downtown, which makes addresses easy to read.

sections.h2: When is Littleton property tax due?
sections.html:
Because Littleton spans three counties, the due dates come from the county that bills the parcel, and most of the city is in Arapahoe County. Jefferson County, which covers a small portion, lists 2026 deadlines of March 2 and June 15 for two installments, and April 30 for a single full payment.

Jefferson County sends the only tax notice by the end of January, and a payment due on a Friday or weekend is accepted the next business day without interest. Its treasurer's office is at 100 Jefferson County Parkway in Golden. The Jefferson County dates page has the full calendar.

At closing, a title company prorates the year's bill between you and the buyer, so the figure you see on the settlement statement should match the parcel's county record.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Littleton house work?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Littleton works the same as anywhere in Colorado, minus the lender. We review the property, make an offer, and a title company handles the deed and recording with the county that holds the parcel.

We buy houses as they are, with tenants or without, and with open repairs. That helps owners of older houses that need updates, owners of small rentals who are ready to exit, and heirs managing a property from out of state.

faqs.q: What county is Littleton, CO in?
faqs.a: Littleton is the county seat of Arapahoe County, and most of the city lies there. Small portions extend into Jefferson County and Douglas County.

faqs.q: Is a Littleton mailing address always inside Littleton city limits?
faqs.a: No. The Littleton name is used on eleven ZIP codes that cover a much larger area, including unincorporated communities like Columbine, Ken Caryl and Roxborough Park. Use the city's Address Wizard to check a specific house.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a rental property in Littleton?
faqs.a: If you own a property with three or more residential units inside city limits, yes. The annual fee is $75 for 3 to 25 units and $125 for 26 or more, and the license renews by April 1.

faqs.q: What happens to a Littleton rental registration when I sell?
faqs.a: The seller should notify the city of the upcoming change of ownership, and the new owner must register within 30 days of the transfer.

Most of the Arapahoe County portion is in Littleton Public Schools, which runs Heritage, Littleton and Arapahoe high schools. Other portions fall in Sheridan, Englewood, Jeffco and Douglas County districts.
